newsitem.title: USA: US mortgage-backeds rise with T-notes, await FOMC.
newsitem.headline: US mortgage-backeds rise with T-notes, await FOMC.

text.p: U.S. mortgage-backed securities rose modestly during a quiet Monday session, with spreads over Treasuries a whisker wider ahead of Tuesday's Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting, traders said.
Late Monday, pass-throughs were unchanged to 7/32 higher overall, while comparable Treasuries were up 6/32 to 9/32.
Many market participants said they expect the central bank will vote to boost the federal funds target rate by 25 basis points to 5.50 percent.
"The consensus is that we get 25 (basis points)," said one Collateralized Mortgage Obligation (CMO) trader.
If the Fed's policy-making arm votes to increase interest rates, the Treasury yield curve will flatten and push CMO buyers down the curve, causing CMO yield spreads to widen, he said.
Similarly, pass-through yield spreads may widen under the same scenario, another trader said.
However, if the Fed decides to hold interest rates steady, the Treasury yield curve would probably steepen, prompting a rally in mortgages, traders said.
"The curve would steepen ... that would be great for mortgages," one head trader said.
In key coupons, Ginnie Mae 30-year 7.5 percent paper was up 6/32 at 98-30/32, yielding 98 basis points over the 10-year Treasury note.
Comparable Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac issues were 6/32 higher as well, at 99-01/32 and 99-07/32, respectively.
The 10-year note was up 9/32 at 96-22/32 bid, yielding 6.71 percent.
The latest Reuters survey showed 34 of 48 economists polled were expecting the Fed to tighten short-term interest rates on Tuesday.
